items.title: Alvin Alcorn Interview, 1976-01-25
items.q: We had a bass player around. He was a lot of bass player. I was kind of Randy Jackson.

ctx.x: Do you think that sound being deadened has a bad effect on music? Do you think it causes music not to grow as well? No, I don't think so.

Because it keeps it closer to me, you know, you got to go where it's at. Mm-hmm. You know? And just like we used to could hear a woodhouse, a wood coming out. We could always tell when the parade was coming. We could hear the bass tuba. Mm-hmm. That was really, you know, penetrated over anything. And the drums. And we could hear that beat coming three or four blocks before the music would get near. Yeah. And we knew it was coming from some direction, like the drums and things. They'd come in and play the drums…
You know, this took me over time. Sure.
